svg.title: Style & editing
svg.desc: Precision: “The fee excludes students on tight budgets” is clearer than “It is really, really bad”. Use words accurately. Qualify claims when needed: can, may, some. Avoid unsupported “everyone” or “always”. Controlled persuasion: Vary pace: longer sentences explain; short sentences emphasise. “Neither sounds spectacular. Both matter.” Use emotion proportionately. A brief example can be more convincing than a dramatic exaggeration. Sentence boundaries: Comma splice: “It is free, everyone can try it.” Repair with a full stop, a semicolon between complete clauses, or a conjunction: “It is free, so everyone can try it.” Punctuation & grammar: Colon after a complete clause introduces explanation. Apostrophe marks possession or omitted letters. Its = possession; it’s = it is/has. Their = possession; they’re = they are. Check agreement and tense. Meaning first: Does every paragraph add a distinct idea? Have you explained how or why with a concrete detail? Does the order make sense? Does the ending fulfil the task? Keep the tone suitable when disagreeing. Accuracy pass: Check sentence boundaries, spelling, apostrophes, tense and agreement. Use spellings printed in the task correctly. Replace vague repetition with an example. Keep checking time for both responses; do not perfect only the first.
